newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bekaa votes in final round of Lebanon election.
newsitem.headline: Bekaa votes in final round of Lebanon election.

text.p: Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley votes on Sunday in the final round of parliamentary elections that have so far returned a strong majority of supporters of the pro-Syrian government.
The Bekaa's 410,000 voters will elect the last 23 deputies to the 128-member parliament in the fifth round of voting that has covered Lebanon's different regions since August 18.

A 23-member pro-government list with six ministers, several sitting deputies and candidates of Hizbollah and Amal -- Lebanon's two main Shi'ite Moslem movements -- is likely to sweep the votes in the Bekaa.
A rival 10-man list of leftists headed by Communist Party chief Farouk Dahrouje and another six-man list may not win a single seat, Beirut political analysts said.

They said Syria, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and a strong military presence in the Bekaa, played a major role in influencing the composition of the government list and even tried to mould the opposition tickets to its liking.
Syrian liaison officers visited Bekaa politicians and politely told them who was acceptable and who was not acceptable on the different lists, political sources in the region said.

The resulting government list is an unlikely group of political rivals, all viewed however as allies of Syria. The aim of making them run together was to avert an open electoral battle in the Bekaa, Beirut analysts said.

The main rivals are the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) and the secular Amal movement. They were also pressed onto a joint list in last week's vote in south Lebanon to avoid bloodshed that might have occurred had they presented rival lists.
Newspapers said the opposition candidate most likely to win a seat was Tarek Habchi, a Maronite Christian representing the town of Zahle on the leftist list.

Habchi, a popular figure in the region, could benefit from indignation among Bekaa Christians that under the Syrian-brokered deal the Maronite on the government list for Zahle was chosen by Hizbollah. The candidate is a nephew of President Elias Hrawi.

Hizbollah has three members and two supporters on the government list. If all win, the Syrian-sponsored deals in the south and the Bekaa will give it a total of seven deputies and two allies in parliament compared with eight deputies and four allies before.

Newspapers say Syria has intervened strongly in the south and the Bekaa because these areas serve as the theatres of Hizbollah's war to oust Israeli troops from Lebanon, and the guerrillas are an important card in the hand Syria is playing in peace moves with Israel.
Syria wants Lebanese election results to show that Hizbollah remains strong in the south and the Bekaa, analysts said.

But Damascus has also used the elections to show Hizbollah the limits of its independence, helping engineer losses by Hizbollah and other Moslem fundamentalist groups in north and central Lebanon and then forcing it into a distasteful alliance with Amal in the south and Bekaa.
